  • Deirdre Hanley
  • Frances H. Arnold
Article23 Sept 2026

elements.title: The gene-regulatory evolution of the human skeleton (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
The gene-regulatory evolution of the human skeleton

Massively parallel reporter assays and human–ape hybrid skeletal cells are used to study the evolution of human cis-regulatory elements (CREs), revealing how differences in CREs have shaped the composition of human skeletal tissue.

  • Yizhi Yan
  • Nadav Mishol
  • David Gokhman
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
The anthropogenic fingerprint on emerging infectious diseases

Emerging infectious disease outbreak risks are ubiquitous worldwide, and highest in landscapes where people, livestock and fragmented natural ecosystems coexist, but detection and data on outbreaks are currently limited by inequalities in healthcare access.

  • Rory Gibb
  • Sadie J. Ryan
  • Colin J. Carlson
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Gravitational torque drives multidecadal variations in length of day (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Gravitational torque drives multidecadal variations in length of day

Multidecadal fluctuations in Earth’s length of day are shown to be driven by gravitational torque and resisted by electromagnetic and topographic forces, improving our understanding of the material properties and dynamics of Earth’s deep interior.

  • Huifeng Zhang
  • Mathieu Dumberry
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Single-nucleus transcriptome-wide association study of human brain disorders (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Single-nucleus transcriptome-wide association study of human brain disorders

Single-nucleus transcriptomics across diverse populations is used to explore how genetic risk for brain disorders affects specific cell types, revealing previously hidden gene–trait associations and conserved, cell-type-specific mechanisms.

  • Sanan Venkatesh
  • Roman Kosoy
  • Panos Roussos
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Lu+ optical frequency references with accuracy verified at the 19th digit (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Lu+ optical frequency references with accuracy verified at the 19th digit

Two independent 176Lu+ single-ion optical clocks achieve fractional frequency uncertainties near 10−19 and agree at 5.7 × 10−19, advancing precision timekeeping.

  • K. J. Arnold
  • M. D. K. Lee
  • M. D. Barrett
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Sequence-encoded hexagonal lattices in multichannel peptide nanofibrils (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Sequence-encoded hexagonal lattices in multichannel peptide nanofibrils

Nine-residue peptides can encode discrete interaction motifs that direct the formation of hexagonal pores, which hierarchically tile into laterally expandable multichannel nanofibrils with defined topology.

  • Jasmina Gačanin
  • Francesca Mazzotta
  • Tanja Weil
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Banking records reveal characteristics of financial abuse (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Banking records reveal characteristics of financial abuse

An analysis of UK banking data reveals that people who reported being victim-survivors of financial abuse experience worse financial outcomes compared with a control group.

  • Anna Trendl
  • Nicola Sharp-Jeffs
  • David Leake
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Hepatocytes promote liver metastasis of pancreatic cancer by providing serine (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Hepatocytes promote liver metastasis of pancreatic cancer by providing serine

Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the liver that lack the enzyme necessary to synthesize serine can reprogram hepatocytes to produce this amino acid, thus promoting tumour growth and survival.

  • Koelina Ganguly
  • Keisuke Yamamoto
  • Alec C. Kimmelman
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: A design approach for bitopic kinase inhibitors (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A design approach for bitopic kinase inhibitors

Detailed analyses of ligand choice, linkage vector and linker length enabled the development of bitopic inhibitors of ABL1 and EGFR kinases, including an ABL1 inhibitor with enhanced activity against resistance mutations and reduced off-target toxicity.

  • Jack W. Stevenson
  • Kevin Lou
  • Kevan M. Shokat
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: A methanogen hydrolase reveals the structure of archaeal peptidoglycan (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A methanogen hydrolase reveals the structure of archaeal peptidoglycan

ArmA from Methanobrevibacter smithii, a dominant member of the human gut microbiome, is identified and characterized as a glycosyl hydrolase specific for cleaving the cell wall of methanogens, revealing an unsuspected chemical structure of archaeal peptidoglycan that includes a previously unidentified sugar.

  • Robert Smith
  • Nika Pende
  • Simonetta Gribaldo
Article23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Reference genomes and fossils revise bat family phylogeny and biogeography (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Reference genomes and fossils revise bat family phylogeny and biogeography

An updated phylogeny of bats is presented, based on new genome assemblies and many ancient fossils and including all known bat families.

  • Ariadna E. Morales
  • Yan Liang
  • Emma C. Teeling
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
mTORC1 drives cell-autonomous astrocyte reactivity in tuberous sclerosis

Reactive astrocytes emerge as a primary consequence of TSC2 loss in tuberous sclerosis complex, implicating glial dysfunction as a primary driver of pathogenesis and highlighting the astrocytes as potential therapeutic targets for tuberous sclerosis complex-related neuropathology.

  • Thomas L. Li
  • John D. Blair
  • Helen S. Bateup
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Targeting ZMYND8 unleashes IL-2 signalling to override T cell exhaustion (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Targeting ZMYND8 unleashes IL-2 signalling to override T cell exhaustion

ZMYND8 suppresses IL-2R–STAT5 signalling by inhibiting p300-mediated transcriptional activation of Il2ra to enforce CD8+ T cell terminal exhaustion, and its deletion boosts effector-like states and markedly enhances antiviral and antitumour immunity.

  • Yan Wang
  • Hao Shi
  • Hongbo Chi
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Anomalous metal and superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Anomalous metal and superconducting phases in rhombohedral graphene

Observations of rhombohedral graphene on a WSe2 substrate at varying temperature, magnetic field and current indicate the presence of regions of gate space with zero-resistance superconductivity alongside others with finite saturation resistance.

  • Anna Okounkova
  • Abigail Sohm
  • Matthew Yankowitz
Article23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Lifespan single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human prefrontal cortex (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Lifespan single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human prefrontal cortex

The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex exhibits non-linear, cell-type-specific transcriptional trajectories characterized by dynamic remodelling during development, relative stability in midlife and selective molecular reactivation in late adulthood.

  • Hui Yang
  • Tereza Clarence
  • Panos Roussos
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Agricultural liming is a carbon sink in the Mississippi River Basin (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Agricultural liming is a carbon sink in the Mississippi River Basin

Century-scale records of agricultural liming and anthropogenic acidity inputs for the Mississippi River Basin show that agricultural liming has acted as a net carbon sink over the past century.

  • Tim Jesper Suhrhoff
  • Christopher T. Reinhard
  • Noah J. Planavsky
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Stacking-induced direct band gap in CVD-grown 1H MoS2 bilayers (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Stacking-induced direct band gap in CVD-grown 1H MoS2 bilayers

Atomically aligned 1H bilayer MoS2 exhibits a direct band gap, enhanced excitonic emission and stronger valley polarization, establishing its potential for advanced optoelectronic and valleytronic applications.

  • Tilo H. Yang
  • I-Tong Chen
  • Yann-Wen Lan
Article23 Sept 2026

elements.title: TRAM promotes Toll-like-receptor-free myddosome signal transduction (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
TRAM promotes Toll-like-receptor-free myddosome signal transduction

TRAM is a regulator of myddosome assembly through dissociating MyD88 from the TLR–TIRAP complex to enable myddosome maturation and durable downstream signal transduction.

  • Daniel Fisch
  • Vaani Ohri
  • Jonathan C. Kagan
ArticleOpen Access23 Sept 2026

elements.title: Lsp2 links mTORC1 to TOP mRNA translation and lifespan in Drosophila (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Lsp2 links mTORC1 to TOP mRNA translation and lifespan in Drosophila

In Drosophila, the protein Lsp2, which is induced by dietary essential amino acids, is a key physiological effector of mTORC1, and mutant flies that lack the Lsp2 gene exhibit reduced translation of TOP mRNAs and improved longevity.

  • Jun Wang
  • Zixin Cai
  • Zongzhao Zhai
Article23 Sept 2026
